ticket.text: My n8n workflow posts 50 videos at once and half of them fail with 'The service is receiving too many requests from you'.

reply:
Hi,

Your workflow is sending faster than Blotato accepts. The fix is to slow it down.

1. That message means too many requests in one minute. Publishing allows 30 a minute.
2. Stop sending to that step for a moment.
3. Then send fewer posts at a time before you turn the workflow back on.
4. If it is an n8n workflow, the Fix My Automation button in Logs can help repair it.

Next step: Add a pause between posts and run the workflow again.
You will know it worked when the workflow runs through with no "too many requests" errors.
Help page: https://help.blotato.com/support/errors

Thanks,
Support

steps.quote: Rate limit exceeded. Upload Media: 30 requests/minute. Publish Post: 30 requests/minute.

steps.text: Stop sending to that step for a moment.
steps.quote: Stop requests to the limited route after `429`.

steps.text: Then send fewer posts at a time before you turn the workflow back on.
steps.quote: Reduce concurrency and request frequency before resuming.

steps.text: If it is an n8n workflow, the Fix My Automation button in Logs can help repair it.
steps.quote: For n8n requests, the dashboard's FIX MY AUTOMATION action helps repair the workflow.

plain.why: The next step could make the customer post the same videos twice. The help page says to check which posts already went out before sending anything again.
more: Step 2 is vaguer than the help page. It leaves out waiting for the retry time.
Step 1 names one limit, but the page lists two that a workflow like this can hit.
